topics.title: The train journey and Satyajit's ruin

concepts.learning_objective: Recall how the collapse of Satyajit's bank stripped him of his wealth and changed his outlook.
Interpret the recurring question 'What now?' as a sign of Satyajit's anxiety about the future.
Recall how Satyajit's detection of a forged cheque began his rise from clerk to accountant.
Evaluate the author's comment on crime, punishment and Satyajit's later change of feeling about the forgerer.

topics.title: Uncle Srinath's letter and the journey to Shantipur

concepts.learning_objective: Explain what Srinath means by 'benediction' and 'daughter crisis' in his letter.
Identify why Satyajit decides to attend the wedding at Shantipur.

topics.title: The welcome and the homage of the village

concepts.learning_objective: Describe how Srinath, his family and the villagers honour Satyajit on his arrival.
Analyse why Satyajit feels like an impostor while enjoying the 'twilight splendour of departed glory'.

topics.title: The dowry demand and the loss of house and pond

concepts.learning_objective: Analyse the irony of the cash dowry demand made of a man who has lost his fortune.
Interpret Satyajit's mortgaging of his house and pond and the story's closing image.
Identify the author and explain how the story is narrated from Satyajit's perspective.
Interpret key expressions, sentence fragments and Indian idiom used in the story.
